title: The Flats
summary: Full-page rain splash over functioning Harbor Phase: elevated transit, floodwalls, automated freight, calm civic UI. The city is efficient rather than ruined.

dialogue.caption: Harbor Phase worked.
That was the problem.

productionNotes: Establish humane, optimized comfort; not apocalypse.

title: The Flats
summary: Matt rides above the floodwall while systems reroute minor tidal flooding and drones solve problems before people react.

dialogue.system: Minor tidal flooding downtown. Route adjusted.

dialogue.caption: The city absorbed inconvenience before anyone had to feel it.

title: The Flats
summary: Matt's infrastructure oversight job is mostly confirming decisions automated systems have already made.

dialogue.system: Drainage obstruction detected. Drone crew dispatched.

dialogue.caption: His job still used the language of responsibility.
Oversight. Continuity. Municipal resilience.

title: The Flats
summary: Matt exits through pleasant managed inland life: continuity payments, human-led novelty events, and students admitting human oversight is mostly symbolic.

dialogue.screen: Your Continuity Payment posts tomorrow. Harbor Phase thanks you for participating.

title: The Flats
summary: Managed adulthood montage: Chris reviews AI code patches, Ryan fixes marine equipment by feel, Kevin saves a concerning tide chart.

title: The Flats
summary: Justin is bored by optimized training; Nicole saves an old Sector 14 offshore expansion record.

dialogue.display: Performance percentile: 96. Recommended recovery protocol generated.

title: The Flats
summary: The group gathers at a pleasant but dead inland bar. Chris states the theme: nobody actually leaves anymore.

dialogue.justin: I’m saying physically I could have passed the rescue cert.

dialogue.kevin: Physical is usually where you start losing arguments.

dialogue.chris: You ever notice nobody actually leaves anymore?

title: The Flats
summary: Chris clarifies that people do not leave in the old life-defining sense; there is nowhere to go.

dialogue.chris: My parents moved three states chasing work before they were thirty.
Everybody we know still lives twenty minutes from high school.

title: The Flats
summary: Runner channels light up with outer shelf and Sector 14 rumors; the old group chat asks if they are going tonight.

dialogue.nicole: Sector 14 isn’t supposed to have a road approach.

title: The Flats
summary: Gear montage: Matt packs practical kit, Chris undercharges equipment, Ryan checks tide, Kevin saves charts, Justin packs rope, Nicole folds maps.

title: The Flats
summary: Full-page ferry lot establishing shot: cheap gear, work lights, headlamps, cars with open trunks, floodwall, tide board, unofficial runner culture.

dialogue.tideBoard: LOW WINDOW: 4 HRS 12 MIN. CROSSING CONDITIONS: STABLE. OUTER SHELF EXPOSURE: HIGH.

dialogue.caption: Nobody looked excited anymore.
In person, the runs felt less like escape and more like work before dawn.

productionNotes: No lanterns. Use headlamps, LEDs, work lights, phone screens, vehicle lights.

title: The Flats
summary: Matt finds Chris with a dead scanner; Ryan stands apart at the flood steps watching exposed darkness.

dialogue.chris: Spiritually, it’s at one hundred percent.

title: The Flats
summary: Ryan watches water; Justin arrives with a casino rumor; Nicole shuts it down.

dialogue.justin: Okay. I’m hearing there’s a casino out there.

dialogue.matt: There is not a casino out there.

title: The Flats
summary: Ryan calls departure and checks footwear; Chris discovers he is underprepared for the trench.

dialogue.ryan: You tell him about the trench?

title: The Flats
summary: Ryan marks a changed crossing hazard; public models are inadequate. A low siren moves runners onto the steps.

dialogue.ryan: North crossing shifted after the storms.

dialogue.kevin: That is not in the public model.

title: The Flats
summary: Sparse descent page: straps, boots, no-signal flicker, Ryan watching water, group stepping onto black exposed seabed.

dialogue.caption: The beginning of the crossing never felt heroic.

title: The Flats
summary: The first mile is bodily and ugly: mud, shells, fishing line, pools, stink, cold. Chris remembers wrong; Ryan corrects him.

dialogue.chris: This is always worse than I remember.

title: The Flats
summary: Walking rhythm develops; Matt checks tide too often; Justin drifts toward audience; Ryan dryly predicts his survival into unbearable status.

dialogue.chris: You checking that every thirty seconds helps the ocean respect you more?

dialogue.matt: It helps me respect me more.

dialogue.kevin: Guy’s gonna get himself swept one night.

dialogue.ryan: He’ll probably survive long enough to become unbearable first.

title: The Flats
summary: Mud gives way to old pavement; Nicole identifies markings as wrong for shoreline access. A work light hints at massive offshore geometry.

title: The Flats
summary: Mostly silent reveal fragments: vertical lines, hard edges, something huge, then fog swallows it. Chris punctures awe with fear.

title: The Flats
summary: Concrete foundations and transit fragments show organized human intent; Sector 14 sign confirms maps have hidden or lost the scale.

dialogue.kevin: They built way farther out than people said.

dialogue.nicole: They built farther out than maps say.

title: The Flats
summary: Justin returns shaken-excited. The flats open wider; Chris senses they are walking somewhere people were not supposed to come back from.

dialogue.chris: You ever get the feeling we’re walking somewhere people weren’t supposed to come back from?

dialogue.ryan: Pretty sure that’s the whole point.

title: The Flats
summary: Slow reveal page: tower, second shape, elevated structure, more mass. The group slows before scale.

title: The Flats
summary: Final splash: vast unfinished offshore district. The group is small between Harbor Phase and a drowned future.

dialogue.caption: What they had imagined as drowned outskirts was something else.
Not a neighborhood.
Not ruins.
A future interrupted before anyone could live in it.
The Reach.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: The group processes the Reach's scale. Ryan focuses on channels, not skyline, and orders them left; Justin looks right.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Outer structures appear. Nicole notes traffic-managed design; Kevin clocks the group is already slow.

dialogue.chris: That makes me feel less safe.

dialogue.kevin: We’re already eight minutes slower than the model.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Runner markings introduce folk navigation: route arrows, timing claims, warnings, profanity. Each character reads them differently.

dialogue.wall: SAFE RAMP ↓ / TIDE HOLD 2H / NO SOUTH ENTRY / FUCK SOUTH ENTRY

dialogue.chris: This is language. This is culture.

dialogue.matt: Nobody is trusting bathroom-wall tide math.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Near Reach opens with flooded decks, dead plazas, distant laughter, and a sagging walkway. Ryan chooses the route.

dialogue.chris: Okay. That’s either people or extremely social ghosts.

dialogue.justin: That looks safe if you don’t think about it.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: They climb a wet ramp. Matt catches Kevin slipping without comment; banter keeps the sequence warm.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Chris finds the Fashion Harbor Center directory. The dead mall opens beneath them: lower levels flooded, upper levels accessible.

dialogue.chris: I take back every bad thing I ever said about malls.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: They enter the fourth level; smell hits first. Ryan warns about lifted tile. An optimistic Future Opening banner hangs crooked.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Large atrium reveal: black water fills lower floors and escalators. Nicole notices a MOVE WITHOUT LIMITS ad and falls silent.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Scattered runner occupation: noodles, sock changes, route arguments, a sleeping runner, distorted speaker music. This is not a festival, but it is alive.

dialogue.runner: That route was dry last week.

dialogue.chris: This is better than inland nightlife.

productionNotes: Only practical lights: work lights, headlamps, LEDs. No lanterns.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Ryan declares a twenty-minute hold despite conflicting time reads. Justin immediately begins wandering.

dialogue.kevin: Seventeen if the wind holds wrong.

dialogue.justin: I am not wandering. I am proceeding locally.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Chris finds a faded Harbor Phase Mariners jacket and the group roasts him.

dialogue.nicole: You look like someone who owns a boat he can’t afford.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Justin returns with a Coming Soon Aquarium District panel; everyone tells him to put it back.

dialogue.sign: COMING SOON / HARBOR PHASE AQUARIUM DISTRICT

dialogue.justin: I’m telling you, this place rules.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: At the railing, the flooded mall still makes sense. Nicole states that everything here was built for people exactly like them.

dialogue.chris: The weird thing is it still makes sense.

dialogue.nicole: Everything here was built for people exactly like us.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Silent detail sequence of food court, kiosks, transit access, half-submerged play area. No signal persists.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Nicole and Kevin interpret offline maps: the mall links to transit. Chris calls it fake city; Nicole corrects him.

dialogue.kevin: That corridor shouldn’t connect to the retail level.

dialogue.nicole: It wasn’t retail-only. It linked to transit.

dialogue.chris: They were doing the whole fake city thing.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Justin finds a luxury apartment leasing display; the promised residences contrast with black floodwater outside.

dialogue.display: HARBOR PHASE EAST / RESIDENCES OPENING SOON

dialogue.justin: They really thought people were gonna live out here.

dialogue.ryan: People think a lot of things before water shows up.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Contradictory runner advice about south bridge forces Ryan to use his own read; Matt follows his decision.

dialogue.runner: South bridge is clear if you’re heading Glass Rail.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: A metallic groan silences the mall. Social life collapses back into flooded structure. Ryan calls time.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: The group packs. Chris keeps the Mariners jacket. Matt gives advice to another runner after glancing toward Ryan.

dialogue.matt: Yeah. Stay above the lower service ramp.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Leaving, they see water where it was dry before. Justin asks if they are coming back; nobody answers fast enough.

dialogue.kevin: That wasn’t here when we came in.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Outside, the mall glows weakly with temporary life. Chris says it almost works; Ryan undercuts the romance.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Fog reveals the Glass Rail. Justin wants up, Kevin warns the window is tight, Nicole sees it connects deeper in.

dialogue.justin: We are absolutely going up there.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Matt asks whether they can make it. Ryan authorizes only the first station; Justin accepts the limit.

dialogue.ryan: To the first station. Not past it.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: They move onto a broken elevated walkway; black water curls below; other runners linger too long behind them.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Single-file crossing toward the rail. Chris's jacket flaps; Justin is quiet; Matt notices Ryan is the one leading.

title: The Dead Mall
summary: Final splash: group crosses from Fashion Harbor Center toward the Glass Rail while the mall glows behind and tide returns.

dialogue.caption: The Reach did not feel empty anymore.
That was the dangerous part.

productionNotes: Prestige comic page; practical lights only; show temporary city life behind them.

title: No Signal
summary: Matt's packed gear by the door shows the Reach reorganizing his time before he admits it.

title: No Signal
summary: Preparation montage repeats with variations: Ryan reads water, Kevin saves charts, Chris has wrong socks, Justin has vertical gear, Nicole has maps, Matt fixes straps.

dialogue.justin: This time I’m prepared emotionally and vertically.

title: No Signal
summary: Repeat crossing: familiar landmarks and private jokes show the impossible becoming routine.

dialogue.chris: This is where I almost died.

title: No Signal
summary: Phones lose signal earlier; the group stops checking. Familiarity has landmarks now.

dialogue.caption: The first time, every shape had been impossible.
By the fourth crossing, impossibility had landmarks.

title: No Signal
summary: Inland rhythm changes: Justin bored by optimized wall, Chris misses contract ping, Kevin checks pressure, Nicole maps, Ryan watches tide.

title: No Signal
summary: Tide culture expands through named routes and warning marks; each character reads names differently.

dialogue.marks: THE LIP / EAST CUT / BATTERY STAIRS / SOFT FLOOR — DO NOT TRUST

dialogue.ryan: It’s people getting lost with confidence.

dialogue.kevin: Repeat behavior is not the same as safety.

dialogue.justin: Which one is the stupid climb?

dialogue.matt: South Teeth. And we’re not doing it.

title: No Signal
summary: A runner asks Matt about Harbor Market. Matt answers with Ryan's small confirmation and likes being useful.

dialogue.matt: Upper deck is. Avoid west corner.

title: No Signal
summary: Harbor Market rises above flooded lower levels. Ryan warns they do not stay past the turn.

dialogue.kevin: How many people can stand on that roof?

dialogue.justin: More than currently standing on it.

dialogue.ryan: We don’t stay past the turn.

title: No Signal
summary: They climb through occupied landings and runner repair culture: socks, tape, straps, food.

dialogue.chris: This place has better healthcare than inland.

title: No Signal
summary: Large establishing page: temporary social world of thirty runners, practical lights, black water below, drowned skyline beyond.

dialogue.caption: Nobody organized anything officially.
That was usually how things happened in the Reach.

productionNotes: No lanterns. Make roof alive through people and practical light.

title: No Signal
summary: The group enters; Chris names it illegal and healthy; Ryan stops Justin from joining climbers.

dialogue.chris: Okay. This is extremely illegal and socially healthy.

dialogue.justin: You don’t know what I was going to do.

title: No Signal
summary: Nicole studies a faded network diagram linking market, rail, mall, aquarium district, residences, and pedestrian loop.

dialogue.nicole: It mattered to whoever drew it.

title: No Signal
summary: A newcomer fails to livestream. No-signal becomes a local norm. Chris notices nobody is half-leaving.

title: No Signal
summary: Chris explains that inland people are always in two places; here there is only here.

dialogue.chris: Inland, everybody’s in two places. Here, there’s only here.

dialogue.matt: Maybe everyone’s just too cold to be boring.

productionNotes: Show behavior: listening, pauses noticed, no feeds. Do not make this a manifesto.

title: No Signal
summary: A younger runner asks Matt for route advice. Matt answers before Ryan; Chris clocks that Matt is becoming useful.

dialogue.youngerRunner: You know the mall route back?

dialogue.matt: East side. Stay above the lower service ramp. Don’t use south bridge.

title: No Signal
summary: Kevin warns people away from a weak west corner too softly; Matt repeats the warning louder and gets obedience.

title: No Signal
summary: Chris retells Fashion Harbor Center as myth; Nicole hears his phrase travel and dislikes the distortion.

dialogue.chris: Saddest food court on Earth. Absolutely worth it.

dialogue.justin: It was huge. Historic. Basically marine archaeology.

title: No Signal
summary: Justin climbs a low ventilation housing. Matt and Ryan make him come down, but he still receives the audience he wanted.

title: No Signal
summary: Quiet social high: Matt advises, Chris jokes, Nicole is listened to, Kevin checks structure, Justin draws attention, Ryan watches water alone.

dialogue.caption: For a while, everyone had a use.

title: No Signal
summary: A probably false outer-sector story circulates. Nicole warns Chris he will make this sound better than it is.

dialogue.storyRunner: Outer Sector guy comes back with a municipal sign bigger than a door.

dialogue.nicole: You’re going to make all this sound better than it is.

title: No Signal
summary: Tide turn: water sounds shift. Ryan calls time. People groan. Matt thinks the monitor says they have more.

title: No Signal
summary: Justin challenges the point of easy; Ryan shuts him down. Matt calls pack-up and nearby runners move too.

dialogue.justin: Easy isn’t really the point though.

title: No Signal
summary: They leave while the roof remains alive behind them. The city is not leaving; the water is arriving.

dialogue.chris: Feels rude to leave before the city does.

title: No Signal
summary: Matt confronts Ryan for being heavy back there; Ryan says Matt almost did not move them.

dialogue.matt: You were kind of heavy back there.

title: No Signal
summary: Ryan gives the chapter warning: they are talking about the Reach like land, but it is only tide absent.

dialogue.ryan: You’re all starting to talk about it like it’s land.

dialogue.matt: It is land. Some of the time.

title: No Signal
summary: The warning silences everyone. Ryan resumes movement with one word.

title: No Signal
summary: The group descends toward the flats. Phones still show no signal; Harbor Phase glows far away; the path home is darker.

title: No Signal
summary: Final splash: group moves from Harbor Market toward fog and home. Leaving now feels like being sent home.

dialogue.caption: The first time, leaving had felt like survival.
This time, it felt like being sent home.
